name: Cassel Lychee-Cardamom Frost
description: A delicately carbonated soda pairing real lychee extract with cardamom oil, producing a drink that is floral, faintly spiced, and cold-finishing. Cassel & Dren is known for minimal ingredient lists and high extract quality.
flavor_profile: Perfumed lychee sweetness, a warm cardamom spice bloom in the mid-palate, and a mentholated frost sensation on the finish that is entirely natural — no added cooling compounds
slogan: Some things are just flowers and cold.
cultural_context: Cassel Frost is the soda served at Tier 3 family gatherings when someone wants to impress without being ostentatious. It reads as expensive without being conspicuous. It's also popular as a palate cleanser between courses at mid-tier restaurants that take their food program seriously.
story_hooks: The 'frost' sensation in Cassel Frost has attracted attention from a corponation biotech division that believes the compound causing it could be synthesized and scaled into a new product line — Cassel & Dren has refused to license it, and strange things have started happening to their supply chain

A Tier 4 food scientist has publicly claimed the frost effect is a mild BCI-adjacent sensory artifact rather than a true physical sensation — Cassel & Dren disputes this, but cannot explain the mechanism themselves

A small batch labeled 'Cassel Frost — Unfiltered' appeared in three Tier 3 specialty stores last month with no distribution paperwork; it tastes noticeably different and no one at Cassel & Dren admits to making it
